title: Build a Star Schema with SCD Type 2
summary: Turn the shop's OLTP tables into a star schema with surrogate keys, a date dimension and an order-line fact table, answer a business question over it, and track customer changes as Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2.

hints.test_dimensions_have_surrogate_keys: Give each dimension an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY surrogate (SQLite assigns 1, 2, 3, ...) and keep the natural key (customer_id, product_id) as an ordinary column. Initial customer rows get valid_from '1900-01-01', valid_to '9999-12-31', is_current 1.
hints.test_dim_date_is_contiguous: Generate every day from MIN(order_date) to MAX(order_date) with datetime.date and timedelta(days=1), not just the days that had orders. date_key is the integer YYYYMMDD and quarter is (month - 1) // 3 + 1.
hints.test_fact_grain_is_order_line: Declare the grain first: one fact row per completed order line. Select from order_items joined to completed orders, with no GROUP BY, and store revenue = quantity * unit_price.
hints.test_fact_foreign_keys_resolve: Look up surrogate keys by joining the natural keys: dim_customer on customer_id (and the order date inside [valid_from, valid_to)), dim_product on product_id. date_key comes from the order date.
hints.test_revenue_query_matches_oltp: Join fact_sales to dim_customer and dim_date on their surrogate keys, GROUP BY country, year, quarter, and ORDER BY year, quarter, revenue DESC, country. Don't touch the OLTP tables.
hints.test_scd2_change_adds_version_and_closes: When an attribute changes, UPDATE the current row to valid_to = as_of, is_current = 0, then INSERT a new row with valid_from = as_of, valid_to = '9999-12-31', is_current = 1. Never overwrite name or country in place.
hints.test_scd2_unchanged_rows_untouched: Compare the incoming (name, country) with the current row's. If they're equal, skip the row entirely: no UPDATE, no new version.
hints.test_scd2_is_idempotent: Only compare against the row WHERE is_current = 1. After the first run that row already holds the new values, so a re-run finds nothing to change.
hints.test_scd2_new_customer_inserted: A customer_id with no current row is new: insert it with valid_from = as_of and count it as inserted.
hints.test_history_preserved_for_old_facts: Old facts keep pointing at the old surrogate key, and the closed row keeps the old country, so history doesn't move. Point-in-time lookup: valid_from <= date AND date < valid_to.
